observations.observation: The target article is commentary published near the cutoff, not a new company disclosure. Its cited 2025 backlog and Q2 EPS figures had been publicly reported earlier; its valuation framing and claim that backlog likely continued to grow in 2026 are not issuer updates.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The live page's article dateline and the supplied RSS publication time differ by several minutes; the supplied capture predates cutoff. The article's P/E and annualization are author calculations, not independently verified here.

observations.observation: The underlying backlog disclosure is dated Feb. 5, 2026, with the reported 2025 backlog measured at year-end. The release gives about $20 billion total and $6 billion product backlog; the supplemental deck gives $14 billion service backlog and prior-year product/service figures of $2.5 billion/$9.6 billion. The displayed product figures imply about a 140% increase; the release's '~2.5x' is a rounded ratio description.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The approximate percentage comparison is arithmetic from rounded company figures. Service backlog includes future service revenue and contracts may be terminated annually for convenience; backlog is not the same as recognized revenue.

observations.observation: The company's July 28 Q2 release reports diluted GAAP EPS of $0.62 versus diluted non-GAAP EPS of $0.78, and raises 2026 revenue guidance to $3.9–$4.2 billion. The article's roughly $0.60 quarterly EPS is close to the GAAP figure; annualizing it is the author's calculation, not company guidance.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The release reports one quarter and a full-year guidance range; neither establishes the result for the full 2026 calendar year.

observations.observation: Independent Axios coverage on Feb. 6, immediately after the annual release, had already connected Bloom's growth narrative to AI power demand and faster on-site deployment while also reporting analyst concerns about competition, supply, and valuation. The AI-demand framing in the Oct. 2 commentary was therefore not newly disseminated there.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: This is secondary coverage and market framing, not a project-level measure of Bloom backlog conversion or customer acceptance.

observations.observation: A material pre-cutoff counterpoint to broad AI-power optimism was reported Sept. 24: Oracle sent a force-majeure notice related to Project Jupiter; the report also described a pipeline delay and a pending air-quality permit for Bloom's planned fuel-cell system. Oracle said the project remained on schedule and Blue Owl said financial commitments were unchanged.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: TechCrunch attributes the first report to Bloomberg. This coverage does not establish a Bloom cancellation, backlog reduction, or revenue/collection change; the underlying notice and permit docket were not checked.

gaps: No official post-February backlog update was verified. The target article's suggestion that backlog likely continued to grow in 2026 remains author speculation in the sources reviewed.
The target article's 380x P/E and valuation arithmetic were not independently reconstructed from point-in-time market data; current live-page quote widgets were excluded.

The article page has no verified update-history or archive record in this research. The pre-cutoff supplied copy is used; the live page's Oct. 2 10:15 PM EST dateline is not reconciled to the supplied RSS timestamp.

The original Bloomberg Project Jupiter report and primary force-majeure notice or relevant state permit docket were not retrieved; TechCrunch provides contemporaneous reporting and quotes Oracle and Blue Owl.
research_notes: Focused on the article's public factual anchors, their original disclosure dates, and a material pre-cutoff project update. The target article is valuation commentary, not an issuer announcement. Its supplied text was captured at 2026-10-03T02:24:38.383206Z, before the 2026-10-03T02:26:30.921846Z cutoff; current dynamic quote widgets and post-cutoff material are excluded. The live article page displays Oct. 2 at 10:15 PM EST, while the supplied RSS message gives 02:21:12Z on Oct. 3; the exact first-publication discrepancy is unresolved, but both precede the cutoff.
